For a journal club, the part worth your time is the middle. Section 1 is where Turing, McCulloch and Pitts, and the "brain as computer" metaphor come in [spya-a8jgf4]. That history is your home ground. The pivot to read closely is his claim that "The brain is not a Turing machine made of meat" [spya-uwxe4h]. You can skim the opening on psychological biases and the Ex Machina material.

Your group will probably want to argue about the essay's structure. He says each of his four arguments "can stand up by itself" [spya-nv6tp0]. He also admits his biological naturalism is "a minority view" [spya-qu7j89].
